learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize.
Acquire the ability to effectively solve problems.
Express oneself correctly in Spanish, both orally and in writing.
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis and processing within their field of application.
Develop the ability to transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Information search and management skill.
Possess the ability to make decisions.
Develop critical reasoning.
Develop the ability to work in a team.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the capacity for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and lifelong learning.
Develop the ability to adapt to new situations.
Become aware of issues related to the environment.
Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer.
Basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Understand and apply the fundamental principles of thermodynamics and heat transfer in industrial systems.
Analyze mass and energy balances in thermal equipment and installations in steady and transient states.
Identify and characterize the different heat transfer mechanisms: conduction, convection, and radiation.
Evaluate the operation and energy performance of thermal machines and systems.
Solve problems related to heat exchangers, thermodynamic cycles, and thermal energy generation and utilization equipment.
Select appropriate calculation methodologies and tools for the analysis of thermal processes.
Interpret and use diagrams, thermodynamic properties, and technical documentation associated with thermal installations.
Consider criteria of energy efficiency, environmental sustainability, and rational use of energy in the design and operation of thermal systems.
Develop critical analysis and problem-solving skills in thermal engineering applied to the industrial field.
Rigorously communicate technical results, calculations, and conclusions related to thermal systems.

syllabus_topics: TOPIC 3: PRINCIPLE 0. THERMAL EQUATION OF STATE AND TEMPERATURE
TOPIC 5: THERMODYNAMIC PROPERTIES OF PURE SUBSTANCES
TOPIC 8: INTRODUCTION TO HEAT TRANSFER. THERMOPHYSICAL PROPERTIES OF MATERIALS
TOPIC 9: ONE-DIMENSIONAL CONDUCTION IN STEADY STATE
TOPIC 11: FINNED SYSTEMS AND ADDITIONAL SURFACES
assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 5/10 is required for Theoretical-Practical Tests 1 and 2. Both Theoretical-Practical Tests 1 and 2 can be retaken in the second sitting. Completion of at least 85% of the Continuous Assessment Tests is required to receive a score in this section. If a student obtains an overall course grade equal to or greater than 5.0 but does not meet one of the minimums established in the evaluation procedures, their overall grade will be 4.9. Grade improvement is not allowed for students who passed the course in the first sitting, nor is the repetition of already passed tests.
